title: Config
description:
Top-level OpenPRX configuration, loaded from `config.toml`.

Resolution order: `OPENPRX_WORKSPACE` (legacy: `OPENPRX_WORKSPACE`) env
→ `active_workspace.toml` marker
→ `~/.openprx/config.toml` (fallback `~/.openprx/config.toml`).

agents.description: Delegate agent configurations for multi-agent workflows.

api_key.description:
API key for the selected provider. No environment variable sets or
overrides it; when it is unset, the key stored for the provider with
`prx auth paste-token --provider <name>` is used.

api_url.description: Base URL override for provider API (e.g. "http://10.0.0.1:11434" for remote Ollama)

auth.description: Auth profile and external credential import settings (`[auth]`).

causal_tree.description:
Decision-plane configuration (`[causal_tree]`).
Default: enabled locally; remote processing remains explicit opt-in.
A versioned `enabled = false` preserves an explicit disable.

channels_config.description: Channel configurations: Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc. (`[channels_config]`).

interaction_notice.text: You are interacting with PRX, an AI system. Its responses may be generated by third-party model providers.

cost.description: Cost tracking and budget enforcement configuration (`[cost]`).

default_model.description: Default model routed through the selected provider (e.g. `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"`).

default_provider.description: Default provider ID or alias (e.g. `"openrouter"`, `"ollama"`, `"anthropic"`). Default: `"openrouter"`.

embedding_routes.description: Embedding routing rules — route `hint:<name>` to specific provider+model combos.

gateway.description: Gateway server configuration: host, port, pairing, rate limits (`[gateway]`).

heartbeat.description: Heartbeat configuration for periodic health pings (`[heartbeat]`).

identity.description: Identity format configuration: OpenClaw or AIEOS (`[identity]`).

identity_bindings.description: Static identity bindings loaded at startup (`[[identity_bindings]]`).

media.description:
Media understanding configuration (`[media]` section).
Controls audio STT and video frame extraction for incoming attachments.

memory.description: Memory backend configuration: sqlite, markdown, embeddings (`[memory]`).

model_routes.description: Model routing rules — route `hint:<name>` to specific provider+model combos.

model_settings.description: Catalog model levels and explicit parameters, keyed by canonical release ID.

plugins.description: WASM plugin runtime switch (`[plugins]`), off by default.

proxy.description: Proxy configuration for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 traffic (`[proxy]`).

query_classification.description: Automatic query classification — maps user messages to model hints.

reliability.description: Reliability settings: retries, fallback providers, backoff (`[reliability]`).

runtime.description: Runtime adapter configuration (`[runtime]`). Controls native vs Docker execution.

scheduler.description: Scheduler configuration for periodic task execution (`[scheduler]`).

security.description: Security configuration: sandboxing, resource limits, audit, tool policy (`[security]`).

skills.description: Skills loading and community repository behavior (`[skills]`).

task_routing.description: Task routing configuration — classifies work by intent before the main agent loop.

tool_tiering.description: Tool tiering configuration — controls which tools are exposed based on intent (`[tool_tiering]`).

tunnel.description: Tunnel configuration for exposing the gateway publicly (`[tunnel]`).

user_policies.description: Static user policy records loaded at startup (`[[user_policies]]`).

webhook.description: Standalone webhook receiver for external event -> topic synchronization (`[webhook]`).

agent_id.description: Stable PRX agent identifier advertised to peers.

card_jwks_uri.description:
Public JWKS URI advertised in the card signature block so peers know where
to fetch the verification key. Defaults to the local JWKS endpoint.

card_signing_key_path.description:
On-disk Ed25519 signing key for the published Agent Card (JWS). When set,
the `/.well-known/agent.json` card is signed and verifiable via the JWKS
endpoint. When unset, an ephemeral per-process key is used (card is still
signed, but the public key only lives for the lifetime of the process).

card_ttl_seconds.description:
Validity window of a published Agent Card, in seconds. Reflected in the
card's `expires_at` and the response `Cache-Control: max-age`.

discovery_advertised.description: Whether to advertise into an external A2A registry.

handoff_nonce_ttl_seconds.description: Replay window for future handoff delegation tokens.

spiffe_strict_validation.description:
When true, a peer that presents an X.509 SVID header but fails chain /
validity / trust-domain verification is rejected. When false (default),
verification failures are logged but fall back to header-asserted trust
(suitable for a trusted front proxy terminating mTLS).

For MCP tool calls, SPIFFE headers (and the fall-back) are considered
only when `gateway.trust_forwarded_headers` is true; otherwise they are
ignored and the caller must authenticate with a bearer JWT.

spiffe_trust_bundle_pem.description:
Trust bundle CA certificate(s) in PEM, used to verify the signature chain
of a peer-presented X.509 SVID. When unset, SVID chain verification is not
performed (only header-asserted issuer allow-listing applies).

trusted_trust_domains.description:
Trust domains accepted when verifying a peer SPIFFE SVID. Empty means the
`allowed_peer_issuers` allow-list is the sole gate (backward compatible).

keep_recent_messages.description: Number of recent non-system messages to keep after compaction.

max_context_tokens.description:
Total model context window in tokens. This uses the same unit as
`RouterModelConfig.max_context`; runtime trigger thresholds subtract
`reserve_tokens` from this total window.

memory_flush.description:
Run memory flush extraction before legacy summary/truncation modes.
Exact `switch` handoffs never invoke a summarizer.

os_paging.description:
Letta/MemGPT-style OS-paging controls (`[agent.compaction.os_paging]`).

Enabled by default (Phase 1). When enabled, oldest messages are evicted
to the durable document store (non-destructively, preserving full
content) and semantically recalled on later turns, instead of being
collapsed into a lossy summary.

reserve_tokens.description: Tokens reserved for the next model response.

AgentCompactionMode.description: Compaction mode for long conversation contexts.

oneOf.description: Disable proactive compaction.

Replace cold context with an exact transcript reference and keep the
durable transcript unchanged.
Conservative compaction that prefers summary replacement.
Aggressive truncation mode for tighter contexts.

compact_context.description: When true: bootstrap_max_chars=6000. Use for 13B or smaller models.

low_priority_tools.description: Tool names treated as low-priority when `priority_scheduling_enabled = true`.

priority_scheduling_enabled.description:
Enables priority scheduling so foreground tool calls run before background batches.
Defaults to false to preserve existing scheduler behavior.

read_only_tool_concurrency_window.description:
Max concurrent read-only tool calls in an iteration batch.
Defaults to 2 to preserve existing scheduler behavior.

log_path.description:
Path to the audit log file, relative to the workspace directory and
kept inside it: a path that could leave it, or a symlink at the file
or its `.lock`, skips audit records with an error (D-055).

max_size_mb.description:
Maximum log size in MB before rotation (at least 1: a size of 0 would
rotate on every record and keep only the last few, so it is refused
at load).

AuthConfig.description: Authentication and external credential import configuration (`[auth]` section).

codex_auth_json_auto_import.description: Automatically import `openai-codex` OAuth credentials from Codex CLI auth.json.

codex_auth_json_path.description: Source path for Codex CLI auth.json import.

AutomixConfig.description: Adaptive escalation policy for cheap-first routing.

cheap_model_tiers.description: Tier markers that identify cheap-first models.

confidence_threshold.description: Escalate when confidence falls below this threshold. Default: `0.7`.

escalation_window_ms.description:
Premium escalation window after the cheap reply, including settlement.
Default: 30,000 ms; allowed range: 1..=120,000 ms.

premium_model_id.description: Premium model target used for escalation.

acknowledge_unrestricted_profile.description:
Operator acknowledgement for an intentionally unrestricted profile.
This suppresses doctor noise only; it does not alter policy behavior.

forbidden_paths.description: Explicit path denylist. Default includes system-critical paths.

max_cost_per_day_cents.description: Maximum cost per day in cents per policy. Default: `500`.

scopes.description: Scope-based tool access control: per-user/channel/chat-type allow/deny rules.

workspace_only.description: Restrict file writes and command paths to the workspace directory. Default: `true`.

AutonomyLevel.description: How much autonomy the agent has

oneOf.description: Read-only: can observe but not act
Supervised: acts but requires approval for risky operations
Full: autonomous execution within policy bounds

BackendSelection.description: Which decision backend runs: `auto` (the factory's order) or one kind.

BrowserComputerUseConfig.description:
Computer-use sidecar configuration (`[browser.computer_use]` section).

The computer-use / agent-browser automation tools were removed (agents use
`shell` instead). Only `api_key` is retained, because the config secret
encryption/migration path still references it.

api_key.description: Optional bearer token (retained only for config secret handling).

BrowserConfig.description:
Browser configuration (`[browser]` section).

The `browser` / `browser_open` automation tools were removed. This section
now only carries `allowed_domains`, consumed by the `web_fetch` tool for
domain validation; `computer_use.api_key` is kept for config secret handling.

allowed_domains.description: Allowed domains for `web_fetch` (exact or subdomain match).

computer_use.description: Computer-use sidecar config (retained only for `api_key` secret handling).

CalibrationProfile.description:
A calibration applied from an evaluation report: the backend kind, the
endpoint and the exact pinned model it was applied to
(`[causal_tree.policy.calibration_profile]`). The endpoint is part of it
(D-094 C-7): two servers that serve one model name do not share a
calibration.

endpoint.description: The endpoint; empty for a backend without one.

calibration_profile.description: The calibration in force, if an operator applied one.

commit_threshold.description: Minimum score to commit a candidate.

extra_latency_budget_ms.description: The extra latency one turn may spend deciding (50 to 5000 ms).

extra_token_ratio_limit.description: Maximum ratio of extra tokens to the turn's baseline tokens.

max_candidates.description: The most candidates a decision considers (1 to 32).

max_decision_hops.description: The most decision hops in one turn (1 to 4).

minimum_choice_confidence.description: Minimum confidence of a Choice answer.

minimum_top_margin.description: Minimum margin between the best two options (0 to 0.5).

CausalTreeConfig.description:
The `[causal_tree]` section.

File and JSON reloads share the same canonical keys and defaults.

enabled.description: Whether the decision plane runs. Default `true`; explicit false is preserved.

schema_version.description:
The schema of this section; 1 is the CDP-PLAN 1.7 schema. Always
written; a file without it predates that schema.

cli.description: Enable the CLI interactive channel. Default: `true`.

whatsapp.description: WhatsApp channel configuration (Cloud API or Web mode).

daemon.description: How this chat process reaches the daemon it borrows channels from.

max_concurrent_visible_turns.description: Maximum concurrent visible provider turns in the TUI Redux driver.

ChatDaemonConfig.description:
Where `prx chat` sends its outbound messages (`[chat.daemon]`).

A chat session opens no IM connection of its own — that would race the
daemon for inbound messages on the same account — so `message_send` in chat
asks the daemon to deliver. That is an ordinary authenticated call to the
daemon's control plane, so it needs the same address and token `prx tasks`
uses.

token.description:
Bearer token for the daemon control plane. Empty sends no credential,
which only works when the daemon runs with `gateway.require_pairing =
false`; otherwise the daemon answers 401 and the send is refused.

url.description:
Base URL of the daemon gateway. Empty (the default) derives it from
`[gateway] host`/`port`, which is right whenever both run on this host.

cooldown_secs.description: Seconds the breaker stays open (1 to 3600).

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failures before the breaker opens (1 to 100).

ClassificationRule.description: A single classification rule mapping message patterns to a model hint.

max_length.description: Only match if message length <= N chars.

min_length.description: Only match if message length >= N chars.

priority.description: Higher priority rules are checked first.

token.description: Cloudflare Tunnel token (from Zero Trust dashboard)

default.text: You are interacting with PRX, an AI system. Its responses may be generated by third-party model providers.

ComposioConfig.description:
Composio managed OAuth tools integration (`[composio]` section).

Provides access to 1000+ OAuth-connected tools via the Composio platform.

api_key.description: Composio API key (stored encrypted when secrets.encrypt = true)

entity_id.description: Default entity ID for multi-user setups

CostConfig.description: Cost tracking and budget enforcement configuration (`[cost]` section).

allow_override.description: Allow requests to exceed budget with --override flag (default: false)

warn_at_percent.description: Warn when spending reaches this percentage of limit (default: 80)

CredentialRefSetting.description: Which credential a decision backend uses. A reference, never a secret.

max_run_history.description: Maximum number of historical cron run records to retain. Default: `50`.

health_url.description: Optional URL to check tunnel health

start_command.description:
Command template to start the tunnel. Use {port} and {host} placeholders.
Example: "bore local {port} --to bore.pub"

url_pattern.description: Optional regex to extract public URL from command stdout

endpoint.description:
The System One endpoint (`compatible_http`, required), or the base
URL that replaces a hosted service's (optional, COORD-6: a hosted
backend stays remote whatever the URL). https, or http on a literal
loopback address; never user information.

max_request_bytes.description: Largest request body (4 KiB to 1 MiB).

max_response_bytes.description: Largest response body (4 KiB to 1 MiB).

model.description:
The model the endpoint serves; one exact version for a hosted
service.

pinned_snapshot.description:
The exact model snapshot a hosted service must answer with (D-043
C-8). OpenRouter requires the exact dated snapshot returned for the
configured model; for TypeSafe it defaults to `model`. Refused for the
other kinds.

remote_enabled.description: Whether decision state may leave this machine. Default `false`.

timeout_ms.description: Transport timeout (10 ms up to the extra latency budget).

record_redacted_projection.description: Whether records keep the redacted state projection.

retention_days.description: Days to keep records (0 follows the fitness retention; at most 3650).

DelegateAgentConfig.description: Configuration for a delegate sub-agent used by the `delegate` tool.

agentic.description: Enable agentic sub-agent mode (multi-turn tool-call loop).

allowed_tools.description: Allowlist of tool names available to the sub-agent in agentic mode.

credential_ref.description:
A credential reference (`cred-<name>`, `prx providers credential
set`) issued for this agent's provider, used instead of an inline
`api_key`. The reference is resolved from the encrypted auth-profile
store only when its owner is this provider; setting both is refused.

identity_dir.description: Optional identity files directory relative to workspace root.

max_depth.description: Max recursion depth for nested delegation

memory_scope.description: Optional memory scope for spawned sessions: "shared" (default) or "isolated".

spawn_enabled.description: Whether this agent is allowed to be targeted by sessions_spawn (default: true).

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt for the sub-agent

DingTalkConfig.description: DingTalk configuration for Stream Mode messaging

allowed_users.description: Allowed user IDs (staff IDs). Empty = deny all, "*" = allow all

client_id.description: Client ID (AppKey) from DingTalk developer console

client_secret.description: Client Secret (AppSecret) from DingTalk developer console

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

allowed_users.description: Allowed Discord user IDs. Empty = deny all.

bot_token.description: Discord bot token (from Discord Developer Portal).

group_reply_mode.description:
Group reply decision mode. When `None` (default), derived from
`mention_only` for backward compatibility (`true => MentionOnly`,
`false => Off`). Set to `smart` to let the model decide per-message
whether to reply or stay silent in guild channels.

guild_id.description: Optional guild (server) ID to restrict the bot to a single guild.

listen_to_bots.description:
When true, process messages from other bots (not just humans).
The bot still ignores its own messages to prevent feedback loops.

mention_only.description:
When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot.
Other messages in the guild are silently ignored.

oneOf.description: Future pairing handshake flow (placeholder; runtime currently falls back to allowlist).
Accept only senders listed in `allowed_from`.
Accept any direct sender.
Ignore direct messages.

allowed_workspace_roots.description: Optional workspace root allowlist for Docker mount validation.

cpu_limit.description: Optional CPU limit (`None` = no explicit limit).

image.description: Runtime image used to execute shell commands.

memory_limit_mb.description: Optional memory limit in MB (`None` = no explicit limit).

allowed_senders.description: Allowed sender addresses/domains (empty = deny all, ["*"] = allow all)

idle_timeout_secs.description:
IDLE timeout in seconds before re-establishing connection (default: 1740 = 29 minutes)
RFC 2177 recommends clients restart IDLE every 29 minutes

EmbeddingRouteConfig.description:
Route an embedding hint to a specific provider + model.

```toml
[[embedding_routes]]
hint = "semantic"
provider = "openai"
model = "text-embedding-3-small"
dimensions = 1536

[memory]
embedding_model = "hint:semantic"
```

api_key.description: Optional API key override for this route's provider

credential_ref.description:
A credential reference (`cred-<name>`, `prx providers credential
set`) issued for this embedding route's provider, used instead of an inline
`api_key`. The reference is resolved from the encrypted auth-profile
store only when its owner is this provider; setting both is refused.

dimensions.description: Optional embedding dimension override for this route

model.description: Embedding model to use with that provider

exploration_rate.description: The exploration rate (0 to 0.10, non-zero only with `read_only`).

oneOf.description: Exploration only among read-only candidates.

FitnessConfig.description: Calendar schedule, evidence thresholds, and retention for fitness v2.

auto_run.description: Run the daily fitness worker in daemon mode.

max_backfill_days.description: Maximum number of closed days recovered after downtime.

min_coverage.description: Minimum available metric weight required to publish a final score.

min_samples.description: Minimum samples required before an evidence-derived subscore is usable.

retention_days.description: Number of daily JSON reports retained on disk.

run_at.description: Local wall-clock time (`HH:MM`) at which the previous day is scored.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to define closed calendar days.

GatewayConfig.description:
Gateway server configuration (`[gateway]` section).

Controls the HTTP gateway for webhook and pairing endpoints.

allow_public_bind.description: Allow binding to non-localhost without a tunnel (default: false)

api_rate_limit_per_minute.description: Max `/api/*` requests per minute per authenticated token.

channel_webhook_dedup_ttl_secs.description:
How long an already-accepted platform webhook delivery (`/whatsapp`,
`/linq`, `/nextcloud-talk`) is remembered so a platform redelivery of the
same payload is answered instead of re-run.

Sized against the sender, not the agent: Meta retries a WhatsApp delivery
for up to 7 days and Linq for ~25 minutes, so a window shorter than the
platform's retry schedule lets a late retry start the turn a second time.

idempotency_max_keys.description: Maximum distinct idempotency keys retained in memory.

pair_rate_limit_per_minute.description: Max `/pair` requests per minute per client key.

paired_tokens.description: Paired bearer tokens (managed automatically, not user-edited)

rate_limit_max_keys.description: Maximum distinct client keys tracked by gateway rate limiter maps.

require_pairing.description: Require pairing before accepting requests (default: true)

trust_forwarded_headers.description:
Trust headers that a reverse proxy in front of the gateway asserts: the
client IP (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`) for rate limiting, and the
caller identity of MCP tool calls (`X-Client-Cert-Subject`,
`X-Forwarded-Client-Cert`, `X-Spiffe-Id`, `X-Spiffe-Svid`,
`X-Client-Cert-Pem`). Disabled by default. Enable only when every request
reaches the gateway through a proxy that removes or overwrites all of
these headers; otherwise any client can claim any identity.

webhook_rate_limit_per_minute.description: Max `/webhook` requests per minute per client key.

oneOf.description: Accept only groups listed in `group_allow_from`.
Accept any group.
Ignore group messages.

GroupReplyMode.description:
How the bot decides whether to reply in a group/guild conversation.

This is orthogonal to [`GroupPolicy`] (which decides *which* groups are
visible at all): `GroupReplyMode` decides, within a visible group, *whether
to speak*. It refines the legacy per-channel `mention_only` boolean.

Backward compatibility: per-channel config carries
`group_reply_mode: Option<GroupReplyMode>`. When `None`, the mode is derived
from the existing `mention_only` flag (`true => MentionOnly`,
`false => Off`), so existing configs behave exactly as before.

oneOf.description:
Never reply to group messages unless explicitly @-mentioned at the
channel layer (equivalent to the legacy `mention_only = false` behavior:
non-@ group messages are dropped at the channel layer as today).
Reply only when the bot is @-mentioned (legacy `mention_only = true`).

Read every group message and let the model decide whether to reply or
stay silent (via the `stay_silent` tool). Only honored for channels that
support smart group-reply (currently Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp).

HeartbeatConfig.description: Heartbeat configuration for periodic health pings (`[heartbeat]` section).

active_hours.description:
Inclusive active hour window `[start_hour, end_hour]` in local time.
Heartbeat ticks outside this range are skipped.

interval_minutes.description: Interval in minutes between heartbeat pings. Default: `30`.

prompt.description: Prompt used by heartbeat worker when dispatching tasks.

allowed_contacts.description: Allowed iMessage contacts (phone numbers or email addresses). Empty = deny all.

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

IdentityConfig.description:
Identity format configuration (`[identity]` section).

Supports `"openclaw"` (default) or `"aieos"` identity documents.

aieos_inline.description: Inline AIEOS JSON (alternative to file path)

aieos_path.description: Path to AIEOS JSON file (relative to workspace)

text.default: You are interacting with PRX, an AI system. Its responses may be generated by third-party model providers.

mention_only.description: When true, only process channel/group messages that mention the bot.

username.description: Username (defaults to nickname if not set)

LarkConfig.description:
Lark/Feishu configuration for messaging integration.
Lark is the international version; Feishu is the Chinese version.

allowed_users.description: Allowed user IDs or union IDs (empty = deny all, "*" = allow all)

app_id.description: App ID from Lark/Feishu developer console

app_secret.description: App Secret from Lark/Feishu developer console

encrypt_key.description: Encrypt key for webhook message decryption (optional)

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

port.description:
HTTP port for webhook mode only. Must be set when receive_mode = "webhook".
Not required (and ignored) for websocket mode.

use_feishu.description: Whether to use the Feishu (Chinese) endpoint instead of Lark (International)

LarkReceiveMode.description:
How OpenPRX receives events from Feishu / Lark.

- `websocket` (default) — persistent WSS long-connection; no public URL required.
- `webhook`             — HTTP callback server; requires a public HTTPS endpoint.

allowed_senders.description: Allowed sender handles (phone numbers) or "*" for all

from_phone.description: Phone number to send from (E.164 format)

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

signing_secret.description: Webhook signing secret for signature verification

access_token.description: Matrix access token for the bot account.

allowed_users.description: Allowed Matrix user IDs. Empty = deny all.

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

room_id.description: Matrix room ID to listen in (e.g. `"!abc123:matrix.org"`).

allowed_users.description: Allowed Mattermost user IDs. Empty = deny all.

channel_id.description: Optional channel ID to restrict the bot to a single channel.

mention_only.description:
When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot.
Other messages in the channel are silently ignored.

thread_replies.description:
When true (default), replies thread on the original post.
When false, replies go to the channel root.

workspace_servers.description:
Which new servers a workspace `mcp.json` may add (D-085 F-1). A
workspace file may always narrow a server defined here (leave it out,
or expose fewer of its tools); anything else it says about such a
server is ignored. `off` (the default) adds nothing, `http_only` adds
HTTP servers, `stdio` adds HTTP and stdio servers (a stdio server is a
program run as PRX's user). Widening this is a high-risk change.

allow_tools.description: Optional allow-list of exposed tools (empty = all)

tool_name_prefix.description: Prefix used in tool naming and routing

url.description: URL for HTTP mode (streamable HTTP endpoint)

working_dir.description:
Working directory of a stdio server (absolute). Unset: a dedicated
empty directory `mcp/<server>` beside `config.toml`, never the
directory PRX was started from (D-088 C-3). Changing it is a launch
change (high risk).

allowed_origins.description: Allowed browser origins for future streamable HTTP clients.

bind.description: Advertised bind address. The gateway may still be started with a CLI port override.

exposed_tools.description:
Tools exposed to external MCP callers.

The defaults are all read-only. Every external MCP caller runs
owner-isolated, so only names on the owner-isolation-aware list
(`crate::tools::execution::OWNER_ISOLATION_AWARE_TOOLS`) can run; any
other name is not advertised, is refused with HTTP 403, and is warned
about at config load. An admissible tool with side effects
(`memory_forget`, `memory_store`, `document_ingest`) is advertised with its real effect by
`GET /mcp/v1/tools/list`, and a retry-safe call of it needs an
`Idempotency-Key`.

jwt_algorithms.description:
Allowed JWT signing algorithms. Symmetric (`HS*`) and `none` are never
accepted; only asymmetric algorithms in this list pass verification.

jwt_audience.description:
Expected `aud` claim for inbound bearer JWTs. When set, the token must
carry a matching audience.

jwt_issuer.description:
Expected `iss` claim for inbound bearer JWTs. When unset, bearer JWT
verification is disabled and bearer tokens are rejected.

jwt_jwks.description:
Inline JWKS document (RFC 7517 JSON) used to resolve signing keys by
`kid`. Takes precedence over `jwt_jwks_uri` and `jwt_public_key_pem`.

jwt_jwks_cache_ttl_secs.description:
Cache lifetime (seconds) for a fetched remote JWKS document. After this
the document is refreshed on the next verification. Defaults to 300s.

jwt_jwks_uri.description:
Remote JWKS endpoint (HTTPS URL) whose document is fetched and cached to
resolve signing keys by `kid`. Used when no inline `jwt_jwks` is set.
Fetching is fail-closed: a network failure with no still-valid cached
copy rejects the token rather than accepting it.

jwt_public_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded public key (RSA/EC/Ed) used when no JWKS is configured.

rate_limit_rps.description:
Per-caller request budget, in requests per second, enforced on
`POST /mcp/v1/tools/call` and keyed by the authenticated owner id.
`0` disables the budget.

require_auth.description: Require an authenticated external identity for mutating calls.

MediaConfig.description:
Media understanding configuration (`[media]` section).

Controls STT transcription for audio and video frame extraction.
Aligns with OpenClaw's media-understanding architecture.

audio_model.description: Audio model name (Ollama model or OpenAI model). Default: "whisper".

audio_ollama_url.description: Ollama base URL for audio transcription. Default: "http://localhost:11434".

max_audio_size_mb.description: Maximum audio attachment size in MiB. Default: 20.

max_video_size_mb.description: Maximum video attachment size in MiB. Default: 50.

video_max_frames.description: Maximum video frames to extract per video. Default: 4.

MemoryConfig.description:
Memory backend configuration (`[memory]` section).

Controls conversation memory storage, embeddings, hybrid search, response caching,
and memory snapshot/hydration.

acl_enabled.description: Feature gate for memory ACL enforcement. Phase 0 keeps this disabled.

archive_after_days.description: Archive daily/session files older than this many days

auto_hydrate.description: Auto-hydrate from MEMORY_SNAPSHOT.md when brain.db is missing

auto_save.description:
Backward-compatible semantic auto-promotion gate.

Message events are controlled by `[memory.events]`; this controls whether
eligible user messages are promoted into long-term semantic memories.

backend.description:
"sqlite" | "lucid" | "postgres" | "markdown" | "none" (`none` = explicit no-op memory)

`postgres` requires `[storage.provider.config]` with `db_url` (`dbURL` alias supported).

conversation_retention_days.description: For sqlite backend: prune conversation rows older than this many days

daily_retention_days.description: For sqlite backend: prune daily rows older than this many days

embedding_cache_size.description: Max embedding cache entries before LRU eviction

keyword_weight.description: Weight for keyword BM25 in hybrid search (0.0–1.0)

legacy_conversation_turns_visible.description:
Phase 1/2 compatibility gate for legacy conversation turns while owner_id
backfill rolls out. Phase 3 can disable and remove this after NULL=0.

lucid_budget.description: Token budget for lucid (replaces ZEROCLAW_LUCID_BUDGET / OPENPRX_LUCID_BUDGET)

lucid_cmd.description: Path to lucid binary (replaces ZEROCLAW_LUCID_CMD / OPENPRX_LUCID_CMD)

lucid_local_hit_threshold.description:
Local hit threshold: minimum number of local results before skipping
remote Lucid recall. (replaces OPENPRX_LUCID_LOCAL_HIT_THRESHOLD)

min_relevance_score.description:
Minimum hybrid score (0.0–1.0) for a memory to be included in context.
Memories scoring below this threshold are dropped to prevent irrelevant
context from bleeding into conversations. Default: 0.4

purge_after_days.description: Purge archived files older than this many days

sqlite_open_timeout_secs.description:
For sqlite backend: max seconds to wait when opening the DB (e.g. file locked).
None = wait indefinitely (default). Recommended max: 300.

sqlite_read_pool_size.description:
For sqlite backend: how many reader connections may be opened.

SQLite allows one writer but genuinely concurrent readers under WAL, so
only reads are pooled. The pool is a connection *reuse* mechanism, not a
concurrency limiter: a caller that finds every reader busy queues for one
instead of failing. Unset derives the size from the available CPUs (see
[`crate::runtime::sqlite_pool::default_read_pool_size`]); if set it must
be greater than 0. Deliberately a separate key from
`channels_config.whatsapp.read_pool_size`, so the two SQLite databases
can be sized independently.

vector_candidate_cap.description:
How many embedded memories one vector recall may score.

Cosine similarity cannot use an index, so the candidate set is bounded
by insertion order (newest first) before scoring; without a bound this
is a full scan of every embedded memory, once per turn. The trade-off is
real and not free: in a store with more embedded memories than this cap,
an old-but-highly-relevant memory is never scored and therefore never
recalled. Raise it to buy recall with latency, lower it to buy latency
with recall. Vector recall logs a warning the first time a recall
actually hits the cap, so a store that has outgrown it says so.

vector_weight.description: Weight for vector similarity in hybrid search (0.0–1.0)

auto_promote_assistant_messages.description: Auto-promote eligible assistant messages. Disabled by default to reduce noise.

auto_promote_user_messages.description: Auto-promote eligible user messages into long-term semantic memories.

min_chars.description: Minimum content length for semantic auto-promotion.

signing_secret.description: Optional HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for `X-Webhook-Signature` verification.

token.description: Required bearer token for incoming webhook events.

ModelOperationSetting.description: The operations a `[[providers.models]]` entry may list.

cache_read.description: Cache read input price per 1M tokens.

cache_write.description: Cache write/creation input price per 1M tokens.

ModelRouteConfig.description:
Route a task hint to a specific provider + model.

```toml
[[model_routes]]
hint = "reasoning"
provider = "openrouter"
model = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514"

[[model_routes]]
hint = "fast"
provider = "groq"
model = "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"
```

Usage: pass `hint:reasoning` as the model parameter to route the request.

api_key.description: Optional API key override for this route's provider

credential_ref.description:
A credential reference (`cred-<name>`, `prx providers credential
set`) issued for this route's provider, used instead of an inline
`api_key`. The reference is resolved from the encrypted auth-profile
store only when its owner is this provider; setting both is refused.

model.description: Model to use with that provider

provider.description: Provider to route to (must match a known provider name)

ModelSettings.description: A model level plus explicit parameter overrides in `[model_settings."<id>"]`.

allow_remote_fetch.description: Allow fetching remote image URLs (http/https). Disabled by default.

max_image_size_mb.description: Maximum image payload size in MiB before base64 encoding.

max_images.description: Maximum number of image attachments accepted per request.

NextcloudTalkConfig.description: Nextcloud Talk bot configuration (webhook receive + OCS send API).

allowed_users.description: Allowed Nextcloud actor IDs (`[]` = deny all, `"*"` = allow all).

app_token.description: Bot app token used for OCS API bearer auth.

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

webhook_secret.description:
Shared secret for webhook signature verification.

Can also be set via `OPENPRX_NEXTCLOUD_TALK_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (legacy: `OPENPRX_NEXTCLOUD_TALK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).

NodeServerConfig.description: Node daemon runtime config used by `prx-node`.

allowed_commands.description:
Command allowlist matched on first token.

In restricted mode this list is required unless explicitly set to `["*"]`.

blocked_commands.description: Command denylist matched on first token. Always enforced.

max_concurrent_tasks.description: Maximum number of concurrent async command tasks.

max_output_bytes.description:
Maximum combined stdout/stderr bytes captured per command and maximum
file read/write payload accepted by the node RPC server.

sandbox_root.description: Sandbox root directory for read/write/cwd constraints.

task_result_ttl_ms.description: TTL for completed task results in milliseconds.

tls_required.description:
Require TLS for non-loopback binds.

When true, node server must either bind to loopback or provide cert/key.

NodesConfig.description: Remote node proxy configuration for core-side RPC calls and node daemon defaults.

request_timeout_ms.description: Default request timeout for node RPC calls.

retry_max.description: Default max retries for node RPC calls.

server.description: Embedded node server defaults used by `prx-node`.

otel_endpoint.description: OTLP endpoint (e.g. "http://localhost:4318"). Only used when backend = "otel".

otel_service_name.description: Service name reported to the OTel collector. Defaults to "prx".

num_ctx.description: Explicit context window sent as Ollama `options.num_ctx`.

OsPagingConfig.description:
Letta/MemGPT-style OS-paging configuration (`[agent.compaction.os_paging]`).

OS-paging is an additive layer for the legacy compaction modes. The exact
`switch` mode bypasses it so paging cannot evict history before a durable
handoff is created. Configuration controls paging thresholds and recall.

eviction_threshold.description:
Token capacity ratio (0.0-1.0, relative to the input window after
subtracting reserved response tokens) above
which eviction is triggered. Letta recommends ~0.70; the legacy
compaction path uses 0.85.

keep_recent_messages.description:
Number of recent non-system messages always retained in the hot window
during eviction (older messages are paged out).

max_recalled_pages.description: Maximum number of evicted pages (document chunks) recalled per turn.

proactive_retrieval.description:
Whether to proactively recall relevant evicted pages on every turn.
When `false`, recall happens only after a context-overflow error.

retrieval_injection_role.description: Role under which recalled pages are injected.

ProviderModelConfig.description:
One `[[providers.models]]` entry: an operator declaration of what one
model of a provider — or every model of it — can do.

It is the curated source of the per-(provider, model) descriptor the
resolver consults. Every field but `provider` is optional and declares
nothing when omitted. A declaration settles what discovery left unknown;
it never lifts what the provider's adapter cannot execute, and negative
catalog evidence still wins over it.

`tool_schema_dialect` and `tool_call_dialect` are the same declarations as
`[[providers.tool_dialects]]` `tool_schema` / `tool_call`, which stays
accepted; one `(provider, model)` may declare a dialect in only one of the
two tables.

context_window.description: The model's context window in tokens.

model.description:
The model (compared ignoring ASCII case), or every model of the
provider when omitted.

native_tools.description: Whether the model accepts native tool calls.

operations.description:
The complete list of operations the model executes; every operation not
listed is unsupported.

provider.description:
The provider, spelled as in `default_provider` (any alias, or a
`custom:<url>` endpoint). Every spelling of one provider identity is the
same provider.

structured_output.description: Whether the model honours a JSON-schema response format.

tool_call_dialect.description:
The textual tool-call grammar the endpoint emits. Entries without
`model` only: the response parser cannot tell models apart.

tool_schema_dialect.description:
The tool-schema dialect the endpoint accepts for this model. Only for a
provider that reads dialect declarations.

vision_input.description: Whether the model accepts image input.

ProviderToolDialectConfig.description:
One `[[providers.tool_dialects]]` entry: what one OpenAI-compatible
endpoint, or one model behind it, accepts.

The entry is the `(provider, optional model)` key plus two capability
fields of the per-(provider, model) descriptor that will replace it (P1-B).
The descriptor now reads this table as operator declarations alongside
`[[providers.models]]` (`tool_schema` / `tool_call` there are
`tool_schema_dialect` / `tool_call_dialect`); the table stays accepted,
and moving its rows into `[[providers.models]]` is a later migration step.

model.description:
The model this entry applies to (compared ignoring ASCII case), or every
model of the provider when omitted.

provider.description:
The provider, spelled as in `default_provider`, `fallback_providers` or
`--provider`: a `custom:<url>` endpoint, or one of the catalog entries
that address a server the operator runs (`vllm`, `llamacpp`,
`lmstudio`, `litellm`). Every spelling of the same provider identity is
the same entry: `custom:http://h:8080/v1/` and `CUSTOM:http://h:8080/v1`
are one endpoint, a different port or path is another.

tool_call.description:
The textual tool-call grammar the endpoint emits. Provider-wide entries
only: the response parser has no model, so a model-scoped grammar would
silently apply to every model of the endpoint.

tool_schema.description: The tool-schema dialect the endpoint accepts.

models.description:
Operator declarations of what a provider's models can do
(`[[providers.models]]`): the curated source of the per-(provider,
model) descriptor the model resolver consults.

tool_dialects.description:
Operator declarations of which tool-schema dialect and which textual
tool-call grammar an OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts
(`[[providers.tool_dialects]]`).

Nothing is inferred from a URL: an endpoint with no entry is offered the
published tool schemas unchanged (`raw`) and only its native
`tool_calls` array is read (`native`).

ProxyConfig.description: Proxy configuration for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 traffic (`[proxy]` section).

all_proxy.description: Fallback proxy URL for all schemes.

http_proxy.description: Proxy URL for HTTP requests (supports http, https, socks5, socks5h).

https_proxy.description: Proxy URL for HTTPS requests (supports http, https, socks5, socks5h).

no_proxy.description: No-proxy bypass list. Same format as NO_PROXY.

ProxyScope.description: Proxy application scope — determines which outbound traffic uses the proxy.

oneOf.description: Use system environment proxy variables only.
Apply proxy to all OpenPRX-managed HTTP traffic (default).
Apply proxy only to explicitly listed service selectors.

QQConfig.description: QQ Official Bot configuration (Tencent QQ Bot SDK)

allowed_users.description: Allowed user IDs. Empty = deny all, "*" = allow all

app_id.description: App ID from QQ Bot developer console

app_secret.description: App Secret from QQ Bot developer console

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

QueryClassificationConfig.description:
Automatic query classification — classifies user messages by keyword/pattern
and routes to the appropriate model hint. Disabled by default.

rules.description: Classification rules evaluated in priority order.

ReadOnlyRehearsal.description: Rehearsal is read-only (CDP 9.3): the only accepted mode.

timeout_ms.description: One rehearsal's timeout (at most the extra latency budget).

ReliabilityConfig.description:
Reliability and supervision configuration (`[reliability]` section).

Controls provider retries, fallback chains, API key rotation, and channel restart backoff.

acknowledge_single_provider_risk.description:
Operator acknowledgement that no provider failover is configured.
This suppresses doctor noise only; it does not add a fallback.

api_keys.description:
Additional API keys for round-robin rotation on rate-limit (429) errors.
The primary `api_key` is always tried first; these are extras.

model_fallbacks.description:
Per-model fallback chains. When a model fails, try these alternatives in order.
Example: `{ "claude-opus-4-20250514" = ["claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "gpt-4o"] }`

provider_backoff_ms.description: Base backoff (ms) for provider retry delay.

provider_retries.description: Retries per provider before failing over.

scheduler_retries.description:
Max retries for cron shell attempts and Agent startup before decision admission.
Admitted Agent turns are not replanned automatically; provider request retries
remain controlled by `provider_retries`.

RemoteNodeConfig.description: A remote node target for core-side node proxy calls.

bearer_token.description: Bearer token for node RPC authentication.

id.description: Stable node ID used by the nodes tool.

RetrievalInjectionRole.description: Where recalled context pages are injected back into the request.

oneOf.description: Inject recalled pages as a leading `system` message (not user-visible).
Inject recalled pages as a leading `user` message.

alpha.description: Similarity score weight. Phase 1 keeps this at `0.0`.

knn_k.description: Number of nearest neighbors considered for voting. Default: `7`.

knn_min_records.description: Minimum history records before KNN affects routing. Default: `10`.

RouterModelConfig.description: Static router metadata for one model candidate.

reserved_output_tokens.description: Output tokens reserved for this model when planning input context.

codex_stream_idle_timeout_secs.description: Codex stream idle timeout in seconds (replaces ZEROCLAW_CODEX_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS)

idle_hang_secs.description:
Seconds an agent turn may produce **no observable progress at all**
before it is judged hung and terminated.

**This is not a turn timeout.** The window is reset by every sign of
life — a provider stream chunk, a tool call starting or finishing,
history compaction, output written to a channel — so a turn that keeps
working runs for as long as it needs to, however long that is. Only
total silence for the whole window counts, which is a stall rather than
a slow task.

Contrast [`RuntimeConfig::long_task_warn_secs`], which measures elapsed
run time, is *not* refreshed by progress, and never terminates anything.
The two must not be conflated or merged: one reports that work is long,
this one recovers from work that is wedged.

Leave unset for the 1800s default; set `0` to disable hang detection
entirely. Enabled values must be at least 30 seconds.

long_task_warn_secs.description:
Seconds after which a still-running work item is reported in the log.

**Notification only — nothing is ever terminated because of it.** PRX
treats long tasks as normal business: a research run or a build can
legitimately take hours, and ending one on a timer is a worse outcome
than letting it finish. This threshold exists so that a task which is
genuinely wedged becomes *visible*, leaving the decision to an operator
(`prx tasks list` / `prx tasks kill`).

Leave unset for the 900s default; set `0` to silence the warning
entirely. Enabled values must be at least 10 seconds, below which the
sweeper would warn about ordinary tool calls.

max_blocking_threads.description:
Hard cap on the tokio blocking-thread pool.

PRX places no ceiling on concurrent turns, sub-agents or sessions, which
makes this pool the last implicit concurrency gate in the process — and
it fails by deadlock, not by rejection: once every slot is held, further
blocking work queues forever with no timeout. Tokio's built-in default
is a hardware-agnostic 512; leaving this unset instead derives the cap
from `available_parallelism()` (cgroup-aware) with a 2048 floor. Raise
it when `[runtime] blocking pool is saturated` warnings appear.

Read during process bootstrap, before the runtime exists, so it takes
effect only on restart — config hot-reload cannot resize a live pool.

reasoning_enabled.description:
Global reasoning override for providers that expose explicit controls.
- `None`: provider default behavior
- `Some(true)`: request reasoning/thinking when supported
- `Some(false)`: disable reasoning/thinking when supported

SchedulerConfig.description: Scheduler configuration for periodic task execution (`[scheduler]` section).

claim_lease_secs.description:
Execution claim lease. Active jobs renew this lease every one third of
the interval; expired claims may be recovered by another scheduler.

max_tasks.description: Maximum number of persisted scheduled tasks.

ScopeConfig.description:
Scope-based tool access control configuration (`[autonomy.scopes]`).

Controls which tools are available per-user, per-channel, and per-chat-type.

Example config:
```toml
[autonomy.scopes]
default = "allow"

[[autonomy.scopes.rules]]
channel = "signal"
chat_type = "group"
tools_deny = ["shell", "file_write"]

[[autonomy.scopes.rules]]
user = "uuid:untrusted-user-uuid"
tools_allow = ["memory_recall"]   # whitelist-only

[[autonomy.scopes.rules]]
channel = "wacli"
send_deny = ["*:+15550001111"]    # never message this recipient
```

assign_owners.description:
Correspondents who own this daemon and may hand work to any `prx chat`
session it knows about.

Entries are `{channel}:{sender}` — the same two-segment shape
`send_allow` uses for a destination, read here as an *origin*. Either
segment may be `"*"`; a bare `"*"` makes every correspondent an owner
and is almost never what an operator wants.

The identity compared here is the runtime-injected `_zc_scope`, not
anything a model or an HTTP body claimed, so an entry names a real
platform account. An owner still loses to a matching `assign_deny`.

Empty (the default) means no correspondent owns this daemon, so the only
way to assign work is an authenticated operator-plane request.

default.description: Default action when no rule matches: "allow" (default) or "deny".

rules.description: Ordered list of scope rules evaluated top-to-bottom.

ScopeDefault.description:
What `autonomy.scopes` does with a tool call no rule matches.

Parsed once, at load: `allow` or `deny` after trimming and ignoring case,
and nothing else (D-050). The runtime (`SecurityPolicy::from_config`) and
the configuration plan (`config::manage::plan`) read this one value, so a
spelling such as `"deny "` can never mean deny to the plan and allow at
runtime. An unknown value is refused when the configuration loads.

oneOf.description: Unmatched tool calls are allowed (the default).
Unmatched tool calls are refused.

ScopeRule.description:
A single scope rule for tool access control.

A rule matches when ALL specified criteria match (logical AND).
Deny always takes priority over allow within a rule.

The two halves of a rule are evaluated differently, on purpose:
* `tools_allow` / `tools_deny` are **first-match-wins** — the first matching
  rule decides tool access and later rules are not consulted.
* `send_allow` / `send_deny` are evaluated over **every** matching rule that
  carries at least one outbound entry, so a rule written for some unrelated
  reason (a `tools_deny`-only rule, say) can never silently swallow a later
  rule's `send_deny`. See `SecurityPolicy::is_outbound_allowed`.

assign_allow.description:
Assignment whitelist: which `prx chat` sessions this scope may hand work
to through `POST /api/chat-sessions/{id}/assign`.

Entries are `{label}:{session_id}` — the same two-segment shape as
`send_allow`, with the live chat session in the place of the recipient.
Either segment may be `"*"`, and a bare `"*"` matches every session. The
label is the human name the chat process registered under, so
`"workstation:*"` follows that chat across restarts while
`"*:{session_id}"` names exactly one run of it.

**The label is self-declared by whoever registered the session.** It is a
convenience for writing rules, not an identity assertion: anything that
can reach the register endpoint can claim any label. Where that matters,
name the session id, which the daemon generates.

Assignment is **default-deny**: with no `assign_owners` and no
`assign_allow` anywhere, no channel correspondent can assign anything.
That is the opposite of `send_allow`, whose empty default still permits
the turn's own channel, and it is deliberate — an assignment starts work
on another entry point, so silence must mean "no".

assign_deny.description:
Assignment blacklist, in the same `{label}:{session_id}` form.

Evaluated across *every* matching rule, so a later `assign_deny` can
never be shadowed by an earlier rule, and it outranks both
`assign_allow` and `autonomy.scopes.assign_owners` — an owner named here
is refused, exactly as `tools_deny` outranks `tools_allow`.

Unlike `send_deny` there is no alias folding: both segments are compared
literally. A chat session id is generated by this daemon and has exactly
one spelling, so there is no alias to fold and no guess to make.

chat_type.description: Match by chat type: "direct", "group", or "*" for any type.

send_allow.description:
Outbound recipient whitelist for `message_send`.

Entries are `{channel}:{recipient}` (for example `"telegram:*"` or
`"wacli:1234@s.whatsapp.net"`); a bare `"*"` matches every destination.
Empty (the default) means this rule imposes no whitelist, so the
same-channel / cross-channel default decides.

The whitelist is matched on the recipient **exactly as written**: unlike
`send_deny`, no alias folding widens it, because widening a whitelist
would grant reach on a guess. The first matching rule with a non-empty
`send_allow` is the one that applies; `validate` rejects a rule whose
`send_allow` an earlier rule would shadow, so this never fails silently.

send_deny.description:
Outbound recipient blacklist, in the same `{channel}:{recipient}` form.

Evaluated before `send_allow`, mirroring how `tools_deny` outranks
`tools_allow`, and evaluated across *every* matching rule so it can
never be shadowed by an earlier one.

The recipient is matched after folding the alias forms that are
derivable from the string itself: a JID's `:device` suffix and server
case (`1234@s.whatsapp.net`, `1234:2@s.whatsapp.net` and
`1234@S.WhatsApp.net` are one person), a leading `+` (`+15550001111`
and `15550001111`), and a UUID's letter case and hyphenation.

**Aliases that are NOT derivable are not covered.** A WhatsApp LID
(`<id>@lid`) carries a different number from the same contact's phone
JID (`<number>@s.whatsapp.net`), and a Signal UUID is unrelated to that
account's E.164 number; correlating either pair needs a mapping table
this layer does not hold. Write one entry per identifier form the
contact can appear under, or deny the whole channel with
`"{channel}:*"`, which is the only form that is alias-proof.

tools_allow.description: Tool whitelist: only these tools are allowed (empty = all tools permitted).

tools_deny.description: Tool blacklist: these tools are denied regardless of allow list.

user.description: Match by sender identity: UUID (e.g. "uuid:xxx"), phone number, or "*" for any sender.

version.description:
The scorer version the weights were chosen for. When set, a scorer of
another version refuses the configuration rather than apply weights
chosen for different scoring.

encrypt.description: Enable encryption for API keys and tokens in config.toml

SecurityConfig.description:
Security configuration for audit logging.

The host-shell sandbox configuration, the former `[security.tool_policy]`
pipeline and the `[security.resources]` command limits were removed: the
first two had no pipeline behind them, and the limits named a per-command
memory/CPU/subprocess ceiling this runtime never enforced and, being an
unbounded runtime, will not. Non-shell tool authorization remains driven by
`[autonomy]`.

workspace_hooks.description:
Whether the command hooks of the workspace `hooks.json` run
(HOOKS-ENV, D-085 O-1). `hooks.json` lives in the agent's workspace,
where the workspace file tools can write it, and each hook runs a
program as PRX's user; so they run only when the operator turns them
`on` here. Turning it on is a high-risk change. WASM plugin hooks are
not affected.

evolution_config_path.description: Path to evolution config file (replaces OPENPRX_EVOLUTION_CONFIG / ZEROCLAW_EVOLUTION_CONFIG)

evolution_debug_raw.description: Enable debug raw output for evolution (replaces OPENPRX_EVOLUTION_DEBUG_RAW / ZEROCLAW_EVOLUTION_DEBUG_RAW)

evolution_interval_hours.description: Evolution scheduler interval in hours (daemon mode).

evolution_judge_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds one evolution judge call may take (1 to 3600, default 180).
A judge that has not answered by then gives no verdict, so an applied
change is rolled back.

fitness_interval_hours.description:
Legacy fitness report interval in hours.

Kept for configuration compatibility. Calendar scheduling is controlled
by `[self_system.fitness]` and this value is no longer used by the
daemon worker.

allow_recursive_delegation.description: Permit an explicitly requested, sealed recursive child grant.

cleanup_on_complete.description: Remove worker workspace directory after process-mode completion.

default_mode.description: Default execution mode for sessions_spawn (`task` or `process`).

max_recursive_depth.description: Maximum additional delegation levels granted to an opted-in child.

process_memory_strategy.description:
Memory strategy for process-mode workers.

Supported values:
- `shared_fabric`: worker uses the parent workspace memory DB.
- `isolated_private`: worker uses its private DB.

worker_workspace_root.description:
Optional root directory for process-mode worker workspaces.

When unset, falls back to `<workspace>/workers`.

account.description: E.164 phone number of the signal-cli account (e.g. "+1234567890").

allowed_from.description: Allowed sender phone numbers (E.164) or "*" for all.

cli_path.description: Path to signal-cli binary. Only used in native mode. Default: "signal-cli" (PATH lookup).

daemon_http_port.description: Local HTTP port for the spawned signal-cli daemon. Only used in native mode. Default: 16866.

daemon_mode.description: Deprecated: ignored. Accepted for backward compatibility with older config files.

data_dir.description:
signal-cli data directory. Only used in native mode.
Default: $HOME/.local/share/signal-cli (signal-cli's standard XDG location).

group_id.description:
Optional group ID to filter messages.
- `None` or omitted: accept all messages (DMs and groups)
- `"dm"`: only accept direct messages
- Specific group ID: only accept messages from that group

http_url.description:
Base URL for the signal-cli HTTP daemon (e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:16866").
In "native" mode this is ignored; the daemon is spawned on `daemon_http_port`.

ignore_attachments.description: Skip messages that are attachment-only (no text body).

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

mode.description:
Channel mode: "native" (spawn signal-cli daemon locally) or "rest" (external daemon/Docker).
Default: "rest" for backward compatibility.

startup_timeout_ms.description: Startup readiness timeout in milliseconds for native `signal-cli` daemon mode.

abnormal_threshold.description: Non-user event threshold within `abnormal_window_secs` before tripping the breaker.

abnormal_window_secs.description: Sliding window in seconds for non-user event counting.

breaker_duration_secs.description: Circuit breaker duration in seconds after threshold is reached.

dedupe_ttl_secs.description: Deduplication TTL in seconds for `(channel + sender + event_type + normalized_content)`.

min_reply_interval_secs.description: Minimum interval in seconds between replies for the same `(channel + reply_target)`.

top_k.description:
How many skills the system prompt may advertise.

The section lists metadata only (instruction bodies stay behind
`skill_read`), so a catalog at or below this size is published whole and
the section becomes a pure function of the installed skills — which is
what keeps the provider's cacheable prefix identical across turns.
Larger catalogs fall back to relevance retrieval, which does move with
the wording; entry points that hold a session narrow that churn with a
session-scoped union (`SessionSkillExposure`).

SkillSuiteRegistration.description: The frozen suite that governs one skill's proposals.

suite_digest.description: SHA-256 digest (64 lowercase hex digits) of the frozen suite.

open_skills_dir.description:
Optional path to a local open-skills repository.
If unset, defaults to `$HOME/open-skills` when enabled.

openclaw_skills_dir.description:
Optional path to a local openclaw-skills clone directory.
If unset, defaults to `$HOME/.openprx/openclaw-skills/` when enabled.

SkillsLifecycleConfig.description:
`[skills_lifecycle]`. The defaults leave the lifecycle off, in `draft_only`
mode, with the strongest publication policy.

allow_executable_proposals.description:
Allow proposals that touch executable files. `true` is refused: a
proposal changes `SKILL.md` text only, also for a skill that has
scripts. Reviewed executable revisions (SL11) come from an operator
import, never from the proposer; script generation is a next-phase
package.

enabled.description:
Turns the lifecycle on. Off by default: nothing is offered and no store
is opened.

max_edit_fraction.description: Edit budget of a proposal as a fraction of the skill body, in (0, 1].

max_edit_tokens.description: Edit budget of a proposal, in tokens.

max_proposals_per_cycle.description: Most proposals one cycle may start.

min_cases_floor.description: Smallest `min_cases` a governing suite may declare. Below 3 is refused.

owner_scope.description:
The owner scope whose lifecycle store this installation manages.
Required when `enabled`.

require_holdout.description: A governing suite must have a holdout split. `false` is refused.

storage_dir.description: Store location under the workspace. Only the default is supported.

suites.description:
The frozen suite per skill. Operator-owned: it is the only source of
the suite that governs a proposal.

SkillsLifecycleModeConfig.description: What the lifecycle may do. Mirrors `LifecycleMode`.

oneOf.description: Drafts and reviews only.
Drafts plus evaluation and gating; never publishes.
Publishes an eligible proposal after every gate.

allowed_users.description: Allowed Slack user IDs. Empty = deny all.

app_token.description: Slack app-level token for Socket Mode (xapp-...).

channel_id.description: Optional channel ID to restrict the bot to a single channel.

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

SmartGroupConfig.description:
Token-saving pre-gate for smart group-reply (`[smart_group]`).

The pre-gate runs after source decision admission and before the full agent
loop for smart-mode group messages that do NOT explicitly @-mention the bot.
A 0-token heuristic sends clearly relevant messages straight to the loop;
obvious noise and uncertain messages require a yes/no confirmation from a
resolver-built, physically accounted classifier before silence is allowed.

@-mentions, DMs, and non-smart modes NEVER reach the pre-gate. The pre-gate
is fail-open: any classifier error/timeout enters the loop (it must never
silently drop a message that should have been answered).

classifier_max_context_messages.description:
How many recent conversation turns to feed the classifier as context.
Default: `3`. Bounded to keep the classifier prompt (and cost) tiny.

classifier_model.description:
Model id for the Tier-2 classifier. When empty, the admitted channel
route's model is resolved. Set this to a cheap-tier model id (e.g. one listed in
`router.automix.cheap_model_tiers`) to minimize cost.

classifier_provider.description:
Provider id/alias for the Tier-2 classifier. When empty, the admitted
channel route's provider is resolved for this auxiliary call.

classifier_temperature.description:
Sampling temperature for the classifier call. Default: `0.0` (the
decision should be deterministic).

classifier_timeout_secs.description:
Per-call timeout (seconds) for the Tier-2 classifier. On timeout the
pre-gate fails open (enters the loop). Default: `5`.

StorageProviderConfig.description: Storage provider backend configuration (e.g. postgres connection details).

connect_timeout_secs.description:
Optional timeout in seconds for *establishing* a connection to a remote
provider. Defaults to 15s when unset.

This bounds the TCP/startup handshake only. Statement execution is never
bounded (no `statement_timeout` is applied) because long-running queries
are normal for agent workloads.

db_url.description:
Connection URL for remote providers.
Accepts legacy aliases: dbURL, database_url, databaseUrl.

pool_max_size.description:
Maximum number of pooled connections for remote providers.

The pool exists for connection *reuse*, not to throttle work: a caller
that finds the pool saturated queues for a connection rather than
failing. Size it against the database's own `max_connections` budget,
not against expected task concurrency.

StorageProviderSection.description: Wrapper for the storage provider configuration section.

StreamMode.description: Streaming mode for channels that support progressive message updates.

oneOf.description: No streaming -- send the complete response as a single message (default).
Update a draft message with every flush interval.

funnel.description: Use Tailscale Funnel (public internet) vs Serve (tailnet only)

default_intent.description: Fallback intent when no rule matches.

rules.description: Rules evaluated in descending priority order.

intent.description: Route intent to apply when a keyword matches.

model_hint.description: Optional model hint/raw model for non-delegated requests.

priority.description: Higher priority rules are checked first.

sub_agent_model.description: Optional raw sub-agent model override for delegated tasks.

allowed_users.description: Allowed Telegram user IDs or usernames. Empty = deny all.

draft_update_interval_ms.description: Minimum interval (ms) between draft message edits to avoid rate limits.

group_reply_mode.description:
Group reply decision mode. When `None` (default), derived from
`mention_only` for backward compatibility (`true => MentionOnly`,
`false => Off`). Set to `smart` to let the model decide per-message
whether to reply or stay silent in groups.

interrupt_on_new_message.description:
When true, a newer Telegram message from the same sender in the same chat
cancels the in-flight request and starts a fresh response with preserved history.

mention_only.description:
When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot in groups.
Direct messages are always processed.

stream_mode.description: Streaming mode for progressive response delivery via message edits.

ToolCallDialectSetting.description: The tool-call grammars an operator may declare for an endpoint.

oneOf.description: Only the native `tool_calls` array is a tool call (the default).

Additionally read `<function=NAME>{json}</function>` from the content,
for a tool name the request registered.

ToolSchemaDialectSetting.description:
The tool-schema dialects an operator may declare for an endpoint.

`gemini` and `anthropic` are deliberately absent: they name the fixed
rewrite of a provider family, which the constructed provider already
reports, and declaring one for a single model of an endpoint would make
argument validation looser than the document that model was shown.
Adding a stripping dialect here would make the model-less
`OpenAiCompatibleProvider::tool_schema_dialect` (still read by callers
that do not know the model) answer `Raw` for endpoints that mix it with
undeclared models; callers that know the model are exact.

oneOf.description: The published document, byte for byte (the default).

The endpoint rejects `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` at the root of a tool
schema: a root `allOf` of plain object fragments is merged losslessly,
and a request carrying any other root combinator fails before transport.

ToolTieringConfig.description:
Tool surface policy consumed by capability publication and decision admission.

Explicit exclusions take precedence over direct-publication preferences.
The selected decision constrains the tools supplied to each model call.

always_exclude.description: Tool names excluded from capability publication.

always_include.description: Tool names preferred for direct publication, subject to admission gates.

channel_exclude.description:
Tool names hidden from IM channel sessions only, on top of `always_exclude`.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_CHANNEL_EXCLUDED_TOOLS`]; set to `[]` to expose the
full operator surface on channels again.

model_allowlists.description:
Optional exact-model tool allowlists. When a model key is present, only
matching tools from the decision-selected set are exposed.

TunnelConfig.description:
Tunnel configuration for exposing the gateway publicly (`[tunnel]` section).

Supported providers: `"none"` (default), `"cloudflare"`, `"tailscale"`, `"ngrok"`, `"custom"`.

WacliConfig.description:
wacli (official) channel configuration.

Connect OpenPRX to WhatsApp via the **official** `steipete/wacli` real-time
interface: inbound via `sync --webhook` (signed HTTP POST) and outbound via
the `wacli send` CLI. The legacy self-maintained JSON-RPC daemon (`host` /
`port`) is no longer supported.

Deployment (run alongside PRX, e.g. a systemd user service):
```text
wacli sync --follow \
  --webhook http://127.0.0.1:16868/wacli \
  --webhook-secret <SECRET> \
  --store ~/.wacli
```

Example TOML:
```toml
[channels_config.wacli]
webhook_listen = "127.0.0.1:16868"
webhook_path = "/wacli"
webhook_secret = "<SECRET>"     # must match --webhook-secret
store_dir = "/prx_workspace/.wacli"
bot_jid = "1234567890@s.whatsapp.net"
bot_number = "1234567890"
self_chat_mode = true
allowed_from = ["*"]
group_reply_mode = "smart"
```

allow_unsigned_loopback.description:
Allow processing unsigned requests when bound to a loopback address.
Defaults to false (signature verification required).

allowed_from.description:
Sender JID allowlist. Use `["*"]` to accept all senders.
JIDs look like `1234567890@s.whatsapp.net` for individuals or
`1234567890-1234567890@g.us` for groups.

bot_jid.description: Bot's own JID, used for reply-to-bot mention detection.

bot_lid.description:
The bot's own WhatsApp LID, used for @mention detection inside groups.
Accepts either the bare digits `263767598346470` or the full
`263767598346470@lid` form; a device suffix such as `:3` is stripped.

bot_number.description: Bot's own phone number (digits), used for `@<number>` mention detection.

cli_path.description:
Path to the `wacli` binary used for outbound sends. When `None`, `wacli`
is resolved from `PATH`.

group_reply_mode.description: Smart group-reply mode. When `None`, derived from `mention_only`.

host.description:
REMOVED: legacy JSON-RPC daemon host. Retained only to detect and reject
stale configs with a clear migration error in [`WacliConfig::validate`].

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

outbound_media_workspace_only.description:
Confine **outbound** media markers (`[IMAGE:…]` and friends) to the
workspace again.

Defaults to `false`: a marker may name any path the daemon can read,
because agents attach files from the operator's own working directories.
Set it to `true` to restore the workspace-confined, `O_NOFOLLOW` loader,
after which a marker pointing outside the workspace degrades to literal
text. It changes nothing else: the SSRF policy for `http(s)` sources, the
per-category size caps, byte-derived typing, the private temp copy handed
to wacli, and the `INFO` audit log all apply in both modes.

port.description: REMOVED: legacy JSON-RPC daemon port. See `host`.

self_chat_mode.description:
Treat messages authored by the linked account in WhatsApp's Message
Yourself chat as owner input. Disabled by default. When enabled, PRX
invokes wacli's experimental self-send path and suppresses reply echoes
by their outbound message IDs.

store_dir.description:
wacli store directory passed as `--store` on outbound sends and used as
a read-only chat-title fallback for older webhook payloads.

webhook_listen.description: Address the inbound webhook server binds to (default: "127.0.0.1:16868").

webhook_path.description: HTTP path the webhook server serves (default: "/wacli").

webhook_secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 secret shared with `wacli sync --webhook-secret`. Required
unless `allow_unsigned_loopback` is set.

brave_api_key.description: Brave Search API key (required if provider is "brave")

provider.description: Search provider: "duckduckgo" (free, no API key) or "brave" (requires API key)

port.description: Port to listen on for incoming webhooks.

secret.description: Optional shared secret for webhook signature verification.

WeightOverrides.description:
Scorer weight overrides; each unset weight takes the scorer's default
(D-040 OQ-A7: the scorer owns the defaults and the budget).

WhatsAppConfig.description:
WhatsApp channel configuration (Cloud API or Web mode).

Set `phone_number_id` for Cloud API mode, or `session_path` for Web mode.

access_token.description: Access token from Meta Business Suite (Cloud API mode)

allowed_numbers.description: Allowed phone numbers (E.164 format: +1234567890) or "*" for all

app_secret.description:
App secret from Meta Business Suite (for webhook signature verification)
Can also be set via `OPENPRX_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` (legacy: `OPENPRX_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`) environment variable
Only used in Cloud API mode

group_reply_mode.description:
Group reply decision mode. When `None` (default), derived from
`mention_only` for backward compatibility (`true => MentionOnly`,
`false => Off`). Set to `smart` to let the model decide per-message
whether to reply or stay silent in WhatsApp group chats (`@g.us`).

mention_only.description: When true, only process group messages that mention the bot.

pair_code.description:
Custom pair code for linking (Web mode, optional)
Leave empty to let WhatsApp generate one

pair_phone.description:
Phone number for pair code linking (Web mode, optional)
Format: country code + number (e.g., "15551234567")
If not set, QR code pairing will be used

phone_number_id.description: Phone number ID from Meta Business API (Cloud API mode)

read_pool_size.description:
Concurrent read connections against the Web-mode session database.

The session store is SQLite in WAL mode: readers run in parallel while
writes stay serialised, so this sizes the read side only. When unset the
size is derived from the available CPUs. Must be greater than 0 when
set; a saturated pool makes callers wait, it never fails them.

session_path.description:
Session database path for WhatsApp Web client (Web mode)
When set, enables native WhatsApp Web mode with wa-rs

verify_token.description:
Webhook verify token (you define this, Meta sends it back for verification)
Only used in Cloud API mode

oneOf.description: They do not run (the default); `prx doctor` and `hooks_status` say so.

They run, in a cleared environment and a dedicated directory beside
`config.toml`.

WorkspaceMcpServers.description:
Which new MCP servers a workspace `mcp.json` may add
(`mcp.workspace_servers`).

oneOf.description:
None: a workspace file may only narrow the servers defined in
`config.toml`.
HTTP servers (still refused when they target a private address).

HTTP servers and stdio servers started with a bare launcher from the
fixed list, in the cleared launch environment.

XinConfig.description: Configuration for the xin autonomous task engine (`[xin]`).

adopt_legacy_tasks.description:
Adopt orphaned, stale, non-recurring legacy tasks into lease-managed
goal/step records on startup (FIX-P2-16). Default: false (zero-breakage).

stale_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes after which a running task is marked stale. Default: 60.
